rootCause.summary: Observations show the payment pipeline completed successfully (payment.received -> payment.committed -> payment.succeeded) but the checkout recorded both a failure and a success for the same attempt. Specifically, payment was committed (database:EV-0030) and payment accepted (api:EV-0031), yet checkout emitted checkout.failed (file:EV-0032) while a checkout replica recorded checkout.succeeded (database:EV-0033) at the same timestamp. The conflicting terminal records for attempt PA1 (file:EV-0032 vs database:EV-0033) are not explained by any retrieved source, so the underlying cause of the mismatch cannot be determined from available evidence.
limitations: Terminal records conflict: checkout.failed (file:EV-0032) and checkout.succeeded (database:EV-0033) for the same attempt and timestamp; no retrieved record explains why the primary checkout emitted failure while the replica recorded success.
No service-level trace or message explaining the checkout failure decision path (e.g., error code, exception, or rollback command) was present in the collected logs.

Simultaneous timestamps (2026-09-14T10:00:00.100Z) could indicate a race/replication/ordering issue, but there is no evidence in the sources to attribute the mismatch to a specific mechanism (replication lag, retry, write failure, or compensating action).
Financial/settlement state beyond the recorded 'COMMITTED' decision (database:EV-0030) is not available; downstream settlement or external acquirer records were not provided.

recommendation.reason: No retrieved source explains why the checkout service emitted failure while the replica recorded success; the primary cause must be determined by the checkout service logs or its error reporting.

recommendation.action: Verify ledger commit and downstream settlement for EV-0030 and determine whether a customer charge was finalized; if the payment was captured unintentionally, prepare refund/compensation steps per finance policy.
recommendation.reason: Database evidence shows payment.committed (database:EV-0030) and payment.succeeded (api:EV-0031). Without reconciliation, the system may have recorded a failure while funds were captured.

recommendation.action: Enable or review additional diagnostic logging and tracing to capture the checkout service's decision path (including error codes, exception stacks, and commit identifiers) and ensure trace-id propagation to replica writes.
recommendation.reason: Simultaneous/contradictory terminal records suggest an ordering/replication or decision-path visibility problem; richer diagnostics will allow root-cause identification if this recurs.

recommendation.action: If immediate customer-impact mitigation is required, coordinate finance and support to check whether the customer was charged and notify the customer until reconciliation completes; avoid blind retries of payment.
recommendation.reason: Ledger shows a COMMITTED decision; blind retries could cause duplicate charges. Confirm captured state before acting.
